title: Muni (and regional rail) operations as run: running time against the schedule, trips not operated, day-to-day variability of running time, and arrival-prediction error
purpose: Inputs for observed running times, effective frequency net of trips not run, a travel-time reliability term in path cost, and tempered informed line choice (shared/beta3/net.ts, strategy.ts; build.ts).

sources.dataPeriod: Wednesday 2026-06-10 service day (SFUSD out of school)
sources.method: Actual arrival per trip and stop from the 511 GTFS-RT TripUpdates feed; prediction error (actual minus predicted arrival, s) for the prediction in force each minute in the 30 minutes before arrival. Cal-ITP stores the error array in ascending minutes against a descending minutes array: the pairing was checked against n_tu_accurate_minutes with Cal-ITP's accuracy band (-60 ln(m+1.3) < e < 60 ln(m+1.5)), 20000 of 20000 rows agree only with the reversed pairing.

sources.publisher: Cal-ITP for MTC (mtc_collab_2025/speeds), public bucket calitp-publish-data-analysis
sources.method: Stop arrival times interpolated from GTFS-RT vehicle positions, per trip and day.

Scheduled trips and trips with vehicle positions by route. Used only to check that the route pattern of trips missing from realtime is stable (correlation 0.92 with 2026-06-10 across routes with 40+ trips). Its rt_sched_journey_ratio (1.9 for Muni all day, 1.7 for Caltrain express) counts positions before departure and after arrival and is not a running-time ratio; not used.

sources.publisher: SF Controller / SFMTA via DataSF (Scorecard Measures kc49-udxn, measure 441 "Percentage of scheduled service hours delivered")
sources.method: Filled service hours / scheduled hours, systemwide (operators and vehicles available); "does not take into account missed service due to delays" (SFMTA).

sources.title: Next Generation Customer Information System, Stakeholder Engagement Report (September 2018), survey of 5,810 riders
sources.method: 87% check predicted arrivals before walking to the stop, 79% while walking, 94% while waiting (at least "sometimes"); riders rated prediction accuracy 2.5 of 5; focus groups define a late vehicle as one that does not arrive as predicted.

sources.title: TAG Unit A1.3 User and Provider Impacts (May 2026), section 6
sources.method: Unreliability = variation travellers cannot predict (day-to-day variability and incidents), excluding predictable variation by time of day (6.1.1). Car reliability ratio 0.4 on the SD of travel time (6.3.4). Public transport: lateness against the timetable, valued at 2.5 x in-vehicle time (PDFH; 2.4 for non-rail schemes), with reliability ratio 1.4 on the SD of lateness relative to average lateness (6.5.3-6.5.5); cancellations count the service interval x 1.5 (6.5.7).

sources.title: Batley et al., New appraisal values of travel time saving and reliability in Great Britain
sources.method: Table 12: bus late arrival 2.88 (commute) and 2.52 (other) x VTT; other PT 1.75-2.24; rail 2.76-3.21; car reliability ratio on SD 0.33-0.42.

sources.publisher: TRB, SHRP 2 Reliability Project L17, Gap-Filling Project 5: Guidebook: Placing a Value on Travel Time Reliability (2014)
sources.method: RR = value of SD / value of mean time. Reports: RAND Europe 2004 expert workshop (Netherlands, UK, Sweden) provisional RR 0.8 car, 1.2 bus and train; Swedish ASEK urban transit 1.1; Carrion & Levinson (2012) meta-analysis of studies, averages 0.1 to 1.5 (most 0.7-1.5).

sources.title: Quarterly Service Performance Review; news releases 2026-05-18 and 2026-09-16
sources.method: Customer on-time: share of riders reaching their destination within 5 minutes of the timetable. FY26 Q3 94.4%, FY26 Q4 95%.

sources.publisher: Caltrain, Executive Director's Monthly Reports (May and August 2026)
sources.method: On time = arriving less than 6 minutes late at end-line stations: April 2026 96.1%, July 2026 96.5%; within 10 minutes 98.5% and 98.9%.

sources.title: San Francisco Bay Ferry Releases Reliability and On-Time Performance Data (2025)
sources.method: January 2025: 94.1% of trips on time; 99.8% of trips operated.

sources.title: Gentile, Nguyen & Pallottino, Route choice on transit networks with online information at stops
sources.method: Informed line choice; its full-information limit is what strategy.ts combineInformed computes.

runTime.definition: Sum over a route-period of actual stop-to-stop times / scheduled times for the same consecutive observed stops (first and last stop of each trip excluded; hops > 30 min scheduled or > 4x + 10 min actual dropped). Period by the scheduled time at the trip's first observed stop. 16:30-19:30 records hold two copies of many trips (the UTC-midnight seam: the same trip on two service days); they are split into two chains by following each copy's times against the scheduled increments, and both kept as weekday observations. Route-period ratio shrunk toward its group's by scheduled hours observed (k = 4 h), clamped to 0.85-1.2.

tripsNotOperated.definition: Scheduled weekday trips (GTFS service M11) with no record in the realtime feed, by period of scheduled departure; shrunk toward the period's systemwide share (k = 60 trips) and scaled so the systemwide share equals SFMTA's 12-month 1.34% of scheduled hours not delivered (2026-06-10 itself: 1.02% of trips missing, cable cars excluded). Cut-short trips (nothing observed in the last quarter of the trip) were 0.4-0.5% of daytime trips and are not added separately.

runTimeVariability.definition: Day-to-day SD of the running time of the same scheduled trip between the same two stops, over 15 weekdays (TAG A1.3 6.1.1: excludes predictable variation by time of day). For each trip seen on 6+ days, from every third stop, the run to the first stop at least 5, 10, 20, 40 minutes on (median over days); variance across days, pooled by route and period. Fitted sd = a + b * minutes by group (weighted least squares over the four lengths). Includes incidents and any error in the position-based arrival times (a short run's SD may be inflated by a few tenths of a minute). The model uses each group's all-day fit times a route-and-period multiplier (the route's SDs over the fit's, weighted by runs, shrunk toward 1 with k = 300 runs); the group-and-period fits are shown for reference (some rest on few long runs).
runTimeVariability.withinDayCheck: On 2026-06-10 the SD across trips within a period, at fixed scheduled lengths, was similar: about 1.0 min at 5, 1.4 at 10, 2.1 at 20, 3.3 at 40 minutes for most routes (runtime.json, runSD).

predictions.definition: Error = actual minus predicted arrival (s), for the prediction in force m minutes before the actual arrival; Muni, 2026-06-10, records 16:30-19:30 excluded (seam). bus/metro: every stop but a trip's first; terminal: a trip's first stop. robustSD = 1.4826 MAD.
predictions.sdFitBus: sd(m) ~ 29.5 s * m^0.59 (m minutes ahead; 29 s at 1, 76 s at 5, 115 s at 10, 173 s at 20)

informationRetained.method: Monte Carlo (data/beta3/raw/ops/scripts/infosim2.py): two lines at a stop, headways 5-15 min, perceived cost gaps 1-12 min, waits exponential with mean half the headway (as in strategy.ts), waiting weighed 2. A rider who knows the waits exactly gains G over the frequency-split optimal strategy; one who sees the waits with Muni's measured prediction error (zero-mean normal, sd(m) above) gains 0.77 G. With half the error 0.94, with 1.5x 0.49, with 2x 0.12.

shareConsulting.note: share who check predictions before walking to the stop at least sometimes; an upper bound on any one trip

rail.method: Delay D at the destination: 0 with probability 1-A, else exponential with scale s beyond the timetable; s from Caltrain's two published thresholds (P(D>=6 min), P(D>10 min)), applied to BART's and the ferry's single threshold. mean = A*s, sd = sqrt(2*A*s^2 - mean^2). Per ride, independent of its length (rail delays come from incidents more than from running).

ferry.note: one month (January 2025); threshold assumed 5 minutes as for BART

reliabilityRatio.appliesTo: SD of a ride's running time (minutes), added to its perceived cost as RR x SD in in-vehicle minutes, for every mode
reliabilityRatio.basis: RAND Europe 2004 expert workshop provisional value for bus and train, 1.2 (SHRP 2 L17 guidebook); Swedish ASEK urban transit 1.1; inside Carrion & Levinson's (2012) meta-analytic range. UK TAG values lateness, not SD, for timetabled public transport (2.4-2.5 x IVT on mean lateness, RR 1.4 on its SD): for a ride whose delays are zero-mean normal that is about 2.4 x 0.40 sd + 1.4 x 2.4 x 0.58 sd = 2.9 sd, an upper bound for a frequent service whose riders do not hold to a timetable.
